reason_for_v003: Direct re-read of build/source-interactions-v001.js disproved the v002/v012 manual-latch interpretation. The source runtime never changes the local manual variable after initialization; it is a static boolean derived only from carousel--manual class presence.

browser_policy.required: interaction-capable browser with exactly one synchronized source and one target tab

corrected_carousel_contract: manual is initialized once as c.classList.contains('carousel--manual') and is never assigned again.
go(n) changes index and renders only; it has no byUser/manual parameter.
Prev/next arrow click calls go(...) then start().
Visual dot click calls go(...) then start().
Qualifying pointer swipe calls go(...) then start().

start() always stop()s the existing timer first, then refuses to start only if manual is statically true, reduced-motion currently matches, fewer than two slides remain, or the carousel is disconnected.
Therefore on a non-carousel--manual instance, every successful manual navigation resets/restarts the 4000ms autoplay interval; it does NOT create a permanent manual latch.
On a carousel--manual instance, autoplay is disabled from initialization onward; manual actions still change slides but start() will refuse a timer every time.

mouseenter/focusin stop(); mouseleave/focusout start() unconditionally, so compound hover+focus exit order may restart autoplay while the other pause condition is still active on a non-manual instance.
prefers-reduced-motion change calls start(); turning reduce off can restart autoplay on a connected non-manual multi-slide instance.
Broken-slide drop removes the slide and matching dot, reindexes dot data-go, hides the containing project/proof owner if no slides remain, and stops autoplay when fewer than two slides remain.
